## Table 4. Registration completeness and implied excess nonviolent deaths in 2025 (2022 baseline)



|Scenario                                       | Completeness| Implied nonviolent deaths| Implied excess| Multiple of registered excess|
|:----------------------------------------------|------------:|-------------------------:|--------------:|-----------------------------:|
|A. Illustrative scenarios                      |             |                          |               |                              |
|Registration complete                          |         100%|                     7,364|          1,494|                           1.0|
|No age group below its 2022 level              |          97%|                     7,562|          1,692|                           1.1|
|90% complete                                   |          90%|                     8,182|          2,313|                           1.5|
|Home deaths missed at their 2022 share (16.7%) |          83%|                     8,840|          2,971|                           2.0|
|75% complete                                   |          75%|                     9,819|          3,949|                           2.6|
|B. Completeness implied by the GMS estimate    |             |                          |               |                              |
|GMS excess, lower 95% bound                    |          77%|                     9,504|          3,634|                           2.4|
|GMS excess, central estimate                   |          58%|                    12,705|          6,836|                           4.6|
|GMS excess, upper 95% bound                    |          46%|                    15,875|         10,005|                           6.7|

Implied nonviolent deaths = 7,364 ÷ completeness; implied excess = implied nonviolent deaths − 5,870. In panel A, the second row adds the deaths needed to bring each age group back to its 2022 level (range 180–216). Panel B gives the completeness at which implied nonviolent deaths would match the GMS excess for 7 October 2023 to 5 January 2025, expressed per year. Completeness is measured relative to 2022 registration. If 2022 registration was itself incomplete, true deaths in 2022 and 2025 are both higher by the same proportion.

# Figures quoted in the text but not tabulated

- Accident death rate 2025: 74.5 per 100,000 (8.4 times the 2022 rate of 8.9)
- Male share of 2025 accidents: 89%
- Share of 2022 births delivered in hospital: 95.2%
- 2022 deaths at home: 16.7%; elsewhere outside hospital: 2.1%
- GMS excess per year: 6,836 (95% CI 3,634–10,005)
- Nonviolent death rate per 1,000: GMS 7.2 (5.4–8.9); MoH registered 2025 3.46; ratio 2.1 (1.6–2.6)
- Implied deaths at 83% completeness exceed registered by 20%
